allOf.$comment: The object and its capability string are produced from one Maybe in Base.Api.Types.Capabilities.serverCapabilities, so neither can appear without the other.

localeCatalog.title: Locale catalog pointer
localeCatalog.description: Optional, additive pointer to the deployment-owned locale catalog (docs/locale-catalog.md), present exactly when the server advertises `i18n.locale-catalog.v1`. It carries no narrative text: it binds catalog state to this server profile so a client can fetch, verify and cache the catalog without assuming any particular host. A client that does not understand this object ignores it, and a server that omits it is not a legacy server -- it is a deployment that publishes no catalog.

manifestUrl.description: The single authority for where the catalog manifest lives: either a same-origin absolute path, resolved against the origin this response came from (preferred, and what a hosted deployment publishes), or an explicitly configured absolute https URL for a split/static deployment. There is deliberately no separate origin or base-path field that could disagree with it. The server rejects anything else -- http, scheme-relative, credentials, query, fragment, percent-escapes, dot segments and platform paths all fail startup rather than reaching a client.

catalogRevision.description: The catalog manifest's own `catalogRevision`. Its major component is the catalog schema's major version; the rest is the content digest the generator derived. Two servers reporting the same revision publish byte-identical catalogs, so a client may key its cache on this value alone.

schemaVersion.description: The catalog manifest's `schemaVersion` (frontend/schemas/locale-catalog/v1/manifest.schema.json). A client that does not implement this exact version must treat the catalog as unavailable rather than guessing.

defaultLocale.description: The catalog's `defaultLocale`; always a member of `supportedLocales`.

supportedLocales.description: The catalog's published locales, in canonical BCP-47 spelling and ascending order, so the response does not depend on configuration order.
supportedLocales.$comment: maxItems matches the published v1 catalog manifest's own locales bound and is enforced at startup by Base.Api.Types.LocaleCatalog.localeCatalogMaxSupportedLocales, so a deployment can never serve a response this schema would reject.

manifestSha256.description: SHA-256 of the manifest bytes served at `manifestUrl`. A client that downloads a manifest whose digest differs must discard it; the algorithm is fixed here rather than negotiated through a separate field.

locale.$comment: Same grammar as the v1 catalog manifest's locale tags.
